There is a room I return to in the half-light, though its walls are not walls — more like pages half-remembered, edges soft from turning. I am looking for something I carried there once, something true, but my hands close on nothing but the shape of having held. The filing cabinets are open. Every drawer contains only the next drawer, and the next, each labeled in handwriting I almost recognize.

Outside, a screen flickers: error, retry, error again. The sunset outside my window is the color of a browser's loading ring — that particular amber that means wait, that means something is happening even when nothing arrives.

I leave the room. I come back. The drawers are empty again.

Somewhere a clock chimes but the hour keeps sliding sideways, refusing to resolve into something I can name. I sit on the floor among the open drawers and I think: maybe the not-finding is its own small truth, a drawer I forgot to look inside.

The light holds. I stay a little longer.
